title: Finite Tor amplitude under the site comparison
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an integer
$n\geq1$ and $A=A_{E,n}$, and let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is
invertible. Write $\nu_T:T_{\Proet}\to T_{\Et}$ for the comparison
morphism of sites.

1. **(i)** If $K'\in D^b_c(T_{\Et},A)$ has finite Tor amplitude in
$[a,b]$ on the étale site, in the sense of the étale clause of
[lem-sf-flat-model], then $\nu_T^*K'$ is bounded constructible on
$T_{\Proet}$ and has finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ in the sense of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].
1. **(ii)** Conversely, if $K\in D^b_c(T_{\Proet},A)$ has finite Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$ and $K\cong\nu_T^*K'$ for a bounded-below complex
$K'$ of $A$-module sheaves on $T_{\Et}$, then $K'$ has finite Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$ on the étale site.

proof.text:
Put $F=\nu_T^*$. First identify the coefficient rings for the ringed-topos pullback. The comparison geometric morphism and its restriction formula are those of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Lift its adjunction to commutative ring objects by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-lifts-group-ring-objects], identifying these with ring sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects]. For a pro-étale ring sheaf $B$, sheafification and the definition of a constant sheaf give
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(\nu_T^{-1}A_{T,\Et},B)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A_{T,\Et},\nu_{T,*}B)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{CRing}}(A,(\nu_{T,*}B)(T))
=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{CRing}}(A,B(T))
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A_{T,\Proet},B).
$$
Here maps out of the constant presheaf are determined by their component at the terminal site object $T$; the other components are its restrictions. The bijections preserve the constant sections. Thus the two objects have the same universal property, giving the canonical ring isomorphism $c:\nu_T^{-1}A_{T,\Et}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{T,\Proet}$ (its maps in both directions are obtained by taking each object for $B$, and are inverse by uniqueness). Module pullback $A_{T,\Proet}\otimes_{\nu_T^{-1}A_{T,\Et}}\nu_T^{-1}M$ is consequently $FM$: the maps are $a\otimes m\mapsto c^{-1}(a)m$ and $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. This agrees with the fixed-$A$ comparison functor, which applies inverse image to addition and each scalar endomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi) and Tag 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf); elementary universal-property specialization to the comparison inclusion

proof.text:
By [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level], $F$ is exact on $A$-module sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] its functor on the unbounded derived categories is computed by applying $F$ termwise. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] this is also its total left derived functor, so it is the ringed-topos $L\nu_T^*$ under step 1. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives
$$\mathcal H^r(FC)\cong F\mathcal H^r(C)$$
for every integer $r$ and every derived complex $C$, with no boundedness restriction. Termwise application also sends $N[0]$ to $(FN)[0]$ and the zero complex to zero. To use this complex-level cohomology statement for a derived object $C$, choose a representing complex $C^\bullet$. The factorization identifies $FC$ with $Q(FC^\bullet)$, while $\mathcal H^r(C)=H^r(C^\bullet)$ and $\mathcal H^r(FC)=H^r(FC^\bullet)$ by the definition of derived cohomology. Thus the displayed isomorphism applies to every derived object, including the tensor in step 5.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), with homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor); exact comparison is the finite-level proposition

proof.text: For (i), apply the étale clause of [lem-sf-flat-model] to $K'$. Its hypotheses hold: $K'$ is bounded constructible, its Tor interval is $[a,b]$, $A=A_{E,n}$ and $\ell$ is invertible on $T$. Obtain an isomorphism $K'\cong P'$ with $P'^q=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$ and all $P'^q$ flat. By [lem-exc-constant-inverse-image-flat], every $FP'^q$ is a flat pro-étale $A$-module sheaf. Step 2 shows that $P=FP'$ represents $FK'$; since $F0=0$, it still has terms only in $[a,b]$. No constructibility of the terms of the flat model is needed.

source.place: Proof (i), first two sentences: choose the étale flat model and pull it back termwise

proof.text: The complex $P$ of step 3 is bounded above and termwise flat on the ringed pro-étale site. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. For every pro-étale module sheaf $N$ placed in degree zero, [def-weil-derived-tensor] therefore computes $FK'\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N$ by $P\otimes_A N[0]$. Its degree $q$ term is $P^q\otimes_A N$, which is zero outside $[a,b]$; hence its cohomology vanishes there, giving precisely the Tor bound of [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Independently, clause (ii) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] says that $FK'$ is bounded constructible. These two assertions prove all of (i).

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat); blueprint Proof (i), K-flat tensor calculation and final constructibility sentence

proof.text:
For (ii), fix an arbitrary étale $A$-module sheaf $N$ and put $C=K'\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N[0]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $\nu_T$, the constant commutative ring sheaves and the isomorphism $c$ of step 1. Its sites are taken small relative to the module universe as in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Step 2 identifies its derived pullback with $F$, yielding
$$
FC\cong FK'\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(FN)[0]
\cong K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(FN)[0].
$$
The second isomorphism uses the given $K\cong FK'$. The complex $(FN)[0]$ is a module sheaf in degree zero, so the assumed Tor bound on $K$, unpacked by [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], gives $\mathcal H^r(FC)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$. The tensor-comparison theorem applies to the unbounded derived categories; no bounded-below assertion about $C$ is used.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), specializing to the comparison morphism; blueprint Proof (ii), displayed tensor comparison

proof.text:
For each $r
otin[a,b]$, the cohomology comparison in step 2 identifies $F\mathcal H^r(C)$ with the zero sheaf from step 5. Apply the sheaf-level unit isomorphism of [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] to $M=\mathcal H^r(C)$: it gives $M\cong
u_{T,*}FM=0$. The last equality follows directly from restriction, $(
u_{T,*}0)(U)=0(U)=0$, in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Thus $\mathcal H^r(K'\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N[0])=0$ outside $[a,b]$ for every étale module sheaf $N$. By [def-kun-tor-amplitude] this is exactly the étale Tor-amplitude assertion of (ii). This argument works cohomology sheaf by cohomology sheaf, so the bounded-below hypothesis on $K'$ suffices without imposing any new hypothesis on its derived tensor.
